options.title: Explore physician pace
options.description: Investigate the factors contributing to the slow physician pace, including any systemic issues or resource constraints. This could involve reviewing patient records and consulting with medical staff to understand the challenges they face.
options.local_fit: This option is relevant as it focuses on understanding the root causes of the slow physician pace, which is a key contributing factor to the observed pattern.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If the investigation reveals systemic issues or resource constraints, pressure may shift to the unit leadership. Otherwise, pressure may remain with the physician lead.
options.how_we_would_know: Review patient records and consult with medical staff. Discuss findings and potential solutions in huddles.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the slow physician pace is due to individual factors, we may not need to revisit this option.

options.title: Protect reserve monitored beds
options.description: Implement a process to protect a certain number of monitored beds for acute arrivals, ensuring that CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients have immediate access to a monitored bed upon arrival. This could involve adjusting bed allocation protocols and communicating the importance of this process to all staff.
options.local_fit: This option is relevant as it directly addresses the gap between policy and practice, where CTAS 1 and CTAS 2 patients may not have immediate access to a monitored bed.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the charge nurse to ensure the process is followed. If high bed occupancy persists, pressure may remain with the charge nurse to find solutions.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor bed occupancy and CTAS patient access. Discuss findings and adjustments in huddles.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the process successfully ensures immediate access, we may not need to revisit this option.

options.title: Improve communication with patients
options.description: Implement a process to communicate expected wait times to patients after rooming, ensuring they are aware of potential delays and the reasons for them. This could involve providing information leaflets or displaying wait time information on screens in the waiting area.
options.local_fit: This option is relevant as it addresses the long waits after rooming, which can impact patient experience and satisfaction.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Pressure may shift to the charge nurse or front desk staff to ensure communication processes are followed. If long waits persist, pressure may remain with these roles to find solutions.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor patient complaints and satisfaction surveys. Discuss challenges and successes in huddles.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the communication process reduces complaints and improves satisfaction, we may not need to revisit this option.

recommendation.rationale: Protecting reserve monitored beds (O2) is recommended as it directly addresses the gap between policy and practice.
recommendation.would_change_if: If the slow physician pace is found to be a significant issue, we may need to prioritize addressing it first.

suggested_reviewers.why: Unit leadership can provide insights into systemic issues and help implement process adjustments.
Medical staff can provide insights into the challenges they face and potential solutions.
